newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says no ratcheting up of US-Canada dispute.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says no ratcheting up of US-Canada dispute.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday the United States was not "ratcheting up" farm trade tensions with Canada with an announcement it would continue to monitor imports of Canadian wheat.
"There's no ratcheting up of friction," Glickman told reporters.
Glickman said the announcement of continued U.S. monitoring was intended to prevent development of any disruptive surges in the U.S. grain trade.
"We remain concerned about any surges," he said, but it was unclear if Canadian shipments would reach the 1.5 million tonne trigger point.
"There is nothing unusual in what we said today...We're being prudent in being sure that a lot of our concerns are addressed early on."
Canada was expected to harvest a huge wheat crop, as was the world overall while U.S. supplies eased only slightly.
